rationale:
Evidence. Iteration 2 (kp 8.0, kd 0.2) raised progress to 0.18 on the oval, 0.10 on the s-bend and 0.085 on the slalom, and scored 49.78. Iteration 3 (kp 6.0, kd 0.2) fell back to progress 0.12 / 0.04 / 0.10 and scored 36.05. Progress therefore tracks proportional gain, and kp 6 is clearly too weak. Steering oscillation at kp 8 was 0.13 to 0.15, above the 0.10 I had hoped for at kp 6, but the kp 6 run did not reduce it enough to justify keeping that lower gain. The oval max_error stayed near 0.06 to 0.066 at both gains, so the standing offset is not yet resolved. All runs still end off_track with one line-loss event.

Change. kp goes from 6.0 back to 7.0, midway between the two raced points, with kd kept at 0.2. This follows the Evaluator's branch (b): progress has dropped below the kp 8 level, so return toward kp 7 and keep kd at 0.2. Geometry, base_speed, ki and line_loss are unchanged, so the race isolates the gain step.

Expected result. Progress near 0.15 to 0.18 on the oval, steering_oscillation between about 0.10 and 0.14, and max_error near 0.06.

Hypotheses and next steps. (a) If progress holds near the kp 8 level and oscillation stays at or below about 0.13, keep kp near 7 and move to sensor geometry: set sensor_size to 0.016 to reduce the centre-sensor dead band against the 25 mm tape. (b) If progress is still below about 0.15 on the oval, the gain is not the main limit, so test sensor geometry (sensor_size 0.016) at kp 8. (c) If the robot tracks the line with no off-track event but completion_time exceeds 3 s, raise base_speed to 1.6 in a later single-group revision.

Measurements wanted: progress and max_error per track, steering_oscillation, line_loss_events, completion_time, and rms_error, so I can separate offset from oscillation.
